materials.title: What Is a Narrative Text?
materials.content:
## Definition

Narrative is a text that tells a story which aims to entertain the audience. It has elements such as plot, characters, and point of view. It consists of orientation, complication, and resolution. It often uses past tense.

### Structure

| Part | What it does | Example from Little Red Riding Hood |
|---|---|---|
| Orientation | Introduces the characters, the setting, and the situation | A mother sends Little Red Riding Hood through the forest to her sick grandmother. |
| Complication | A problem appears and the characters face it | She talks to the wolf, and the wolf runs ahead and swallows Grandmother. |
| Resolution | The problem is solved and the story ends | A woodsman hits the wolf; Grandmother comes out and they have cake and tea. |

### Language features

- Past tense: gave, said, met, ran, swallowed, came.
- Time connectives: one day, on the way, then, when, as soon as.
- Direct speech: 'Where are you going little girl?' he asked.
- Specific characters: Little Red Riding Hood, the Big Bad Wolf, the woodsman.
- Descriptive words that build the picture: sick, biggest smile, ear-piercing scream.

### Intrinsic elements

- Theme: the main idea the story wants to share.
- Characters: the people or animals who act in the story.
- Setting: where and when the story happens.
- Plot: the events from orientation to resolution.
- Point of view: who tells the story.
- Message or moral value: what the audience can learn.

A fractured story keeps the story you already know but changes one or more elements. Shrek is a famous example: it uses the plot points of classic fairy tales, a damsel in a tower guarded by a dragon, and an ogre as the hero, then repeatedly diverges from the traditional plot.

terms.definition: A text that tells a story in order to entertain the audience.
The opening part that introduces the characters, the setting, and the situation.
The part where a problem or conflict appears and the characters must deal with it.
The part where the problem is solved and the story ends.
An element inside the story itself, such as theme, characters, setting, plot, and point of view.
The perspective from which the story is told, for example the wolf's point of view.
A familiar story that is retold with some elements changed, such as the setting, the characters, or the ending.

materials.title: Reading: One Story, Two Versions
materials.content:
## The traditional version

One day, Little Red Riding Hood's mother gave her a basket with some cake inside and told her to walk through the forest to the other side where her grandmother lay sick in bed. Her mother told her not to talk to strangers. On the way she met the Big Bad Wolf, who asked where she was going, and she forgot the rule and answered him. The wolf took a shortcut, swallowed Grandmother whole, put on her cap and nightgown, and climbed into her bed. When the girl arrived, she noticed the big ears, the big eyes, and the big teeth. The wolf jumped out of bed and chased her, but a man chopping wood heard her, hit the wolf over the head with his axe, and Grandmother popped out of his mouth. Then the woodsman, the girl, and Grandmother all had cake and tea.

| Part | Traditional version |
|---|---|
| Orientation | A mother sends her daughter through the forest with cake for a sick grandmother. |
| Complication | The girl talks to the wolf; the wolf swallows Grandmother and waits in her bed. |
| Resolution | A woodsman saves the girl, Grandmother comes out of the wolf's mouth, and they share cake and tea. |

## The fractured version: the wolf's point of view

The fractured version is titled Little Red Riding Hood: A Fractured Fairy Tale and is told by the wolf himself. The wolf is packing up his troubles in the woods when he hears a twig snap. He meets a Little Red Hooded Teen who is chewing gum, holding a smartphone, and carrying a basket that says 'Mommy's little girl'. He tries to be friendly and reaches into his pocket for a Friendship Coupon, but instead he pulls out an 'I will eat you' coupon from The Three Thousand Humongous Pigs restaurant.

The girl screams an ear-piercing scream and calls him an armadillowolf. A troop of seven dwarves appears; they call themselves the Seven Levels of Awesomeness and one of them plays a high chord on an electric guitar. The girl hides behind a tree and says she has no job, and the wolf answers that she has a delivery job. Her basket has a label that reads 'To Grandma, 2235 NE Forest Ct.', so the wolf finally knows where Grandmother lives. At the old lady's door he meets his old friend Bobwolf, who is chasing three little pirates.

Inside, Grandmother is so scared that she jumps into the wolf's mouth and he accidentally swallows her. The girl arrives with cookies, and the wolf speaks in his best old lady voice. She notices his big paws, not big ears or big eyes, and realises that humans cannot have paws. She calls him the creepy armadillo wolf who wrote the card that said 'I will eat you'. She shouts for a doctor, and a dwarf in a doctor coat pulls a frog and then a cat out of the wolf's throat, playing on the puns 'a frog in your throat' and 'cat got your tongue'. Finally Grandmother is pulled out, and they all live tax-free ever after.

| Element | Traditional version | Fractured version |
|---|---|---|
| Narrator | A third-person narrator outside the story | The wolf himself, telling his own side |
| Little Red Riding Hood | A polite girl who forgets her mother's rule | A teenager with gum, a smartphone, and a lot of attitude |
| Setting | A forest and a grandmother's house long ago | The same forest and house, with modern objects such as a smartphone and a delivery label |
| Main problem | The wolf wants to eat the girl | The wolf wants to make friends and find out what is in the basket |
| Ending | A woodsman saves the girl and Grandmother | A dwarf doctor pulls Grandmother, a frog, and a cat out of the wolf; everyone lives tax-free |

The fractured version keeps the outline of the traditional story: a girl, a basket, a forest, a grandmother, and a wolf. What changes is the narrator, the details of the characters, and the way the problem is solved.

terms.definition: The familiar story that most people know, told in the usual way.
A retelling that changes an element of the familiar story, such as the point of view or the ending.
The perspective of the narrator; in a fractured story it can be moved to another character.
A funny imitation of a familiar story or style.
A joke that plays with two meanings of a word or phrase, for example 'cat got your tongue'.
A statement made larger than reality for a comic effect.

materials.title: Writing a Fractured Story
materials.content:
## Seven ways to fracture a story

A fractured story begins with a story you already know. You do not need to change everything at once. Start with one element, then add more when you feel confident. The checklist in the book lists seven changes you can make.

| Change | What it means | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Change a word in a familiar title | Give the story a new, slightly different name | Little Red Riding Hood becomes Little Red Surfing Hood |
| Insert a new character or swap characters | Add someone new or exchange roles | The woodsman is replaced by a troop of dwarves |
| Change an important object | Replace the object the plot depends on | The basket of cake becomes a basket of cookies |
| Change the setting | Move the story to another place or time | The forest becomes a school corridor |
| Change the point of view | Let another character tell the story | The wolf tells the story himself |
| Change the story resolution | End the story in a different way | The wolf and the girl become friends |
| Use another mode | Add a picture, a comic strip, or a short video | Add a picture for each page of a picture book |

### Keep the structure

Even when the details change, a fractured story still needs orientation, complication, and resolution. The reader must still know who the characters are, what problem they face, and how the problem ends. That is why the writing organizer asks for the traditional version and your version side by side.

| Organizer part | Traditional version | Your fractured version |
|---|---|---|
| Title | Little Red Riding Hood | Little Red Riding Hood: A Fractured Fairy Tale |
| Characters | A girl, her mother, Grandmother, the wolf, a woodsman | A hooded teen, the wolf, seven dwarves, Bobwolf |
| Setting | A forest and Grandmother's house | The same forest with modern objects |
| Problem | The wolf wants to eat the girl | The wolf wants to make friends and see the basket |
| Solution | A woodsman rescues the girl | A dwarf doctor rescues Grandmother |

### From draft to picture book

1. Plan the book: the target audience, the pages, and the sources you need.
1. Write the text with the template: page 1 introduces the characters and setting, pages 2-3 introduce the main conflict, pages 4-7 show the actions and the complications, pages 8-9 present the climax, and page 10 gives the resolution.
1. Illustrate the pages so that the pictures communicate the plot, not only decorate it.
1. Publish the book and review it with a classmate and your teacher.

### Checklist before you publish

- The title gives a clue about the main character or the setting.
- The setting is clear and interesting.
- The events flow from beginning to end with transition words.
- The characters are developed, not only described.
- There are only a few mistakes in grammar and spelling.

To copy the traditional story word for word
To count how many pages the book needs

blocks.explanation: Organizer membandingkan versi asli dan versi baru agar perubahan terlihat jelas dan struktur cerita tetap utuh.

blocks.question: You keep the characters and the setting but let the wolf become friends with the girl. Which change did you make?

choices.text: Change the story resolution
Change the point of view
Insert a new character

blocks.explanation: Mengubah akhir cerita berarti mengubah resolution; tokoh dan latar tetap sama.

nodes.text: Your group retells Cinderella from the stepsister's point of view. Which opening keeps the story recognisable?

choices.text: Introduce the same characters in the same house, seen from the stepsister's side
choices.feedback: Orientation tetap memuat tokoh dan latar yang sama; hanya sudut pandangnya yang berubah.

choices.text: Replace Cinderella with a robot and the house with the moon
choices.feedback: Mengganti tokoh dan latar sekaligus membuat cerita tidak lagi dikenali sebagai Cinderella.

nodes.text: The stepsister says Cinderella never did any chores. What do you do with the original scene where Cinderella works all day?

choices.text: Keep the scene and let the stepsister interpret it differently
choices.feedback: Adegan asli dipertahankan, tetapi ditafsirkan ulang dari sudut pandang tokoh lain; inilah inti cerita pecahan.

choices.text: Delete the scene because it does not fit the new view
choices.feedback: Menghapus adegan penting membuat alur dan masalah cerita hilang.

nodes.text: The class can no longer follow your story. What is the best repair?

choices.text: Keep one or two changes and return the rest to the original story
choices.feedback: Perubahan yang sedikit dan jelas lebih mudah diikuti daripada banyak perubahan sekaligus.

choices.text: Add even more changes so the story is completely new
choices.feedback: Menambah perubahan justru menjauhkan cerita dari versi yang dikenali pembaca.

nodes.text: The draft keeps the original resolution: Cinderella goes to the ball and the prince finds her. The stepsister is sorry. What does your group check before publishing?

choices.text: That the change stays consistent and the message is clear
choices.feedback: Konsistensi sudut pandang dan pesan yang jelas adalah syarat cerita pecahan yang baik.

choices.text: Nothing; a fractured story can change its point of view in the middle
choices.feedback: Perpindahan sudut pandang tanpa alasan membuat pembaca bingung.

nodes.text: Your group's story is confusing. What should you do next?

choices.text: Compare it with the traditional version and revise the missing parts
choices.feedback: Membandingkan dengan versi asli memperlihatkan bagian yang hilang atau berubah tanpa alasan.

choices.text: Publish it anyway and let readers guess
choices.feedback: Cerita yang membingungkan tidak mencapai tujuan menghibur pembaca.

nodes.text: The story now keeps the same characters, setting, and plot, but the stepsister tells it. Your group has made a coherent fractured story.
Readers cannot follow the story, and the changes look accidental rather than chosen.

feedback.correct: Tepat. Unsur cerita dan istilah naratif ini muncul di seluruh bab.
feedback.wrong: Baca ulang Glossary dan bagian Structure, lalu hubungkan setiap istilah dengan satu contoh dari Little Red Riding Hood.

options.text: It is a pun: the dwarf literally pulls a cat out of the wolf's throat.
The wolf really owns a cat as a pet.
The girl refuses to speak to the dwarf.
The cat is the narrator of the story.

questions.explanation: Ungkapan 'cat got your tongue' berarti tidak bisa berbicara; penulis menjadikannya lelucon harfiah.

questions.question: Why does the girl call the wolf an armadillowolf?

options.text: She invents a strange name because she is frightened and confused.
She knows the scientific name of the animal.
The wolf introduces himself with that name.
The narrator uses it to describe the grandmother.

questions.explanation: Sebutan armadillowolf adalah karangan gadis yang panik, bukan nama ilmiah.

questions.question: Why is 'they all lived tax-free ever after' humorous?

options.text: It twists the familiar ending 'happily ever after' into a joke about taxes.
It explains how the characters paid for the cookies.
It is the traditional ending of Little Red Riding Hood.
It shows that the wolf works for the government.

questions.explanation: Penulis memplesetkan frasa penutup dongeng yang lazim menjadi lelucon tentang pajak.

questions.question: What lesson does the traditional version emphasise?

options.text: Children should follow their parents' warning about strangers.
Wolves make the best friends.
Cookies are dangerous for grandmothers.
Shortcuts through the forest save time.

questions.explanation: Karena gadis melanggar pesan ibunya, versi tradisional menekankan pentingnya menaati peringatan tentang orang asing.

questions.question: How does the fractured version change the wolf's character?

options.text: He becomes lonely and wants a friend rather than a meal.
He becomes a woodsman who saves the girl.
He becomes the girl's teacher.
He becomes a dwarf with an electric guitar.

questions.explanation: Serigala versi pecahan berulang kali menyatakan ingin berteman, bukan memangsa gadis.

questions.question: What role do the seven dwarves play in the fractured version?

options.text: They are comic helpers who finally rescue Grandmother.
They are the girl's brothers who send her to the forest.
They are the owners of the restaurant.
They are the narrators of the story.

questions.explanation: Para kurcaci muncul sebagai tokoh lucu; salah satunya berperan sebagai dokter yang mengeluarkan nenek.

questions.question: Why does the wolf swallow Grandmother in the fractured version?

options.text: She jumps into his mouth out of fear, so it happens by accident.
He plans to eat her before the girl arrives.
He mistakes her for a cookie.
The dwarves order him to do it.

questions.explanation: Nenek melompat ke mulut serigala karena ketakutan; serigala menyebutnya kecelakaan.

questions.question: What does adding 'A Fractured Fairy Tale' to the title tell the reader?

options.text: The story is a retelling with deliberate changes to a familiar tale.
The story is a completely new tale with no connection to tradition.
The story is a factual report about fairy tales.
The story is the original version written first.

questions.explanation: Judul memberi sinyal bahwa pembaca akan menemukan versi yang sengaja diubah dari dongeng yang dikenal.

questions.question: Which statement best compares the endings of the two versions?

options.text: Both end with Grandmother safe, but the traditional version uses a woodsman while the fractured version uses a dwarf doctor and puns.
Both end with the wolf eating everyone.
The traditional version ends sadly and the fractured version ends sadly too.
The fractured version has no ending at all.

questions.explanation: Kedua versi menutup dengan nenek yang selamat, tetapi cara penyelesaiannya berbeda.

questions.question: Which detail is an example of exaggeration for comic effect?

options.text: The dwarves call themselves the Seven Levels of Awesomeness.
The story happens in a forest.
Grandmother is sick in bed.
The girl carries a basket.

questions.explanation: Nama 'Seven Levels of Awesomeness' dilebih-lebihkan untuk menimbulkan kelucuan.

questions.question: Which are ways to fracture a story? Choose all that apply.

options.text: Change the point of view
Change the setting
Change the story resolution
Copy the story word for word

questions.explanation: Tiga perubahan pertama membuat cerita pecahan; menyalin tanpa perubahan bukan cerita pecahan.

questions.question: Match each word with its meaning.

options.text: orientation
complication
resolution
pun

map.o0: the part that introduces characters and setting
map.o1: the part where the problem appears
map.o2: the part where the problem is solved
map.o3: a joke that plays with two meanings of a word

questions.explanation: Keempat istilah ini adalah inti bab: tiga bagian struktur cerita dan satu alat humor.

questions.question: Arrange the steps of writing a fractured story.

options.text: Choose a story you know well
Choose one element to change
Complete the narrative organizer
Write the draft
Review and revise the draft
Publish the story

questions.explanation: Cerita dipilih, satu unsur diubah, organizer diisi, draf ditulis, ditinjau, lalu dipublikasikan.
